title: Progressive geo-routing with soft quotas and fast-fail circuit breakers
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Background: As usage grows across multiple regions, we need routing logic that keeps tail latency within SLOs while avoiding hard global ejects that cause unnecessary failovers. Existing approaches either aggressively geo-pin requests (preserving locality but risking overloaded local pools) or use blunt hedging which multiplies load. This ticket designs and implements a progressive geo-routing strategy combining soft per-region quotas, fast-fail circuit breakers, and gradual hedging windows tied to token-level capacity hints.

Goals:
- Maintain 99th percentile inference latency under customer SLO targets during regional load spikes.
- Avoid large-scale cross-region migration that increases inter-region egress and amplifies failures.
- Provide predictable, auditable fallbacks and explainable routing decisions for customer-facing incident notes.
- Enable safe rollout with observability, canarying, and a kill-switch.

Success criteria (release):
- 99p latency regression <= 5% vs baseline under normal load; under regional overload, successful maintenance of latency SLO for >= 95% of requests served by failover policy.
- No more than 10% of traffic hedged globally during steady-state; hedging should only trigger when soft quota breaches persist > 300ms.
- Circuit breaker trips are visible in Console with root-cause tags and automatic degraded-mode routing happens without customer token loss.

Design summary:
1) Soft Quotas: Maintain per-region soft token quotas (derived from reserved capacity + recent autoscaling headroom). Each incoming request is assigned a token-cost estimate (model, sequence length bucket). The region consumes quota; when remaining soft quota falls below configurable thresholds (50%, 20%), routing weight to that region decays smoothly (exponential decay over 5s-60s depending on severity).

2) Fast-fail Circuit Breakers: Two tiers of CBs per region:
   - Latency CB: trips when rolling 1min 99p > region-slo * factor (configurable, default 1.4) and concurrent queueing > threshold.
   - Capacity CB: trips when instantaneous token reservation rate exceeds provisioned token-surge window.
   CBs return a deterministic error code and a suggestion hint (e.g., "TRY_OTHER_REGION" with latency_budget) for caller. Tripped CBs enter a short backoff (exponential, capped) and a sticky decay period where soft-quota decay is accelerated.

3) Progressive Hedging: Instead of immediate hedging to all healthy regions, we apply a progressive hedging window: first try local region (fast path) with a short hedging timeout (50-150ms tunable). If unmet and soft quota below threshold, issue a single hedged attempt to the next best region. If that fails and CBs indicate capacity, escalate to multi-hedge with cost-control safeguards. Hedging aggressiveness is tied to customer tier and token-cost budget.

4) Admission & Degradation Profiler: A runtime admission controller emits degradation decisions (drop, degrade-model, reduce-max-tokens) when global capacity signals hit emergency thresholds. These decisions are signed to the request trace so Console can attribute user-visible regressions to policy actions.

Telemetry & Metrics (required):
- Per-region: soft_quota_total, soft_quota_remaining, quota_decay_rate, circuit_breaker_state{latency,capacity}, trip_count, trip_reason.
- Request-level: route_decision (local/hedged/failover), hedges_issued, hedges_successful, original_latency, final_latency, token_cost_estimate.
- Customer impact: degraded_decision_count, dropped_request_count, degraded_model_fraction.
- Dashboards: SLO burn-down heatmap by region, CB trip timeline correlated with autoscale events, hedging rate trend.

Rollout plan:
- Phase A (staging): implement runtime flags and local simulation harness. Run against replayed traffic for 2 weeks.
- Phase B (canary): enable progressive hedging + soft quotas for 5% of traffic routed by a test routing key; monitor latency, error-rate, egress cost.
- Phase C (ramped): 20% -> 50% -> 100% over multiple cycles with emergency rollback triggers (CB spike, SLO breaches > 3m).

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive hedging reduces tail latency but increases egress and may overload remote pools; soft quotas aim to throttle hedging growth to cap cross-region amplification.
- Fast-fail CBs can increase immediate errors but improve overall user experience by avoiding long tail waits; we return structured hints so upper layers can retry smartly.
- Admission controller complexity vs. predictability: we prefer simpler, auditable degradation steps (drop/degrade/trim) to opaque model rewrites.

Open questions / risks:
- How to unify token-cost estimation across model families with different quantization and batching behavior? Proposal: a small calibration job per model that reports median/90p token processing cost per sequence-length bucket.
- Interaction with Dedicated customer pinning rules: need explicit override semantics and an escape hatch for enterprise SLOs.
- Charging and billing impact of hedging-induced egress—must coordinate with Billing to surface cost attribution.

acceptance_criteria: Soft quotas computed and exported per-region and used in routing decisions
Latency and capacity circuit breakers implemented with observable states and reasons
Progressive hedging path exercised in simulation and canary traffic with documented thresholds
Admission controller emits signed degradation events and Console surfaces them
Rollout plan and rollback playbook documented in Confluence
design_decisions: Use token-cost estimation to normalize capacity across model families
Exponential soft-quota decay to avoid sudden mass ejects
Two-tier CBs (latency + capacity) to capture orthogonal failure modes
Progressive single-hedge first to limit egress amplification
Signed degradation events for auditability and post-incident analysis
telemetry: Implement new metrics with tags: region, model_family, customer_tier
Add SLO burn-down heatmap and CB trip timeline to Console
rollout_plan: Staging simulation using replay for 2 weeks (feature-flagged)
Canary 5% traffic for 48h with automated SLO gates
Ramp 20% -> 50% -> 100% with 1h hold at each step
Rollback triggers: sustained 99p latency > configured SLO by 10% for > 5m
